# Data Analysis

## Prepare for the analysis

### Loading of the libraries

We are using tidyverse framework to rearrange and analysis the data. 

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(broom)
library(data.table)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(forcats)

library("readxl") # read excel files
library("openxlsx")   #The openxlsx package is highly customizable and allows you to: Write multiple data frames to different sheets of the same Excel file. Customize formatting, such as column widths, bold headers, and colors.

library(rmarkdown)
```

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#tidyverse_conflicts()
```


## Read the data

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

filename23_input <- "Data/23_CompositionDataUpdated.xlsx"
filename35_input <- "Data/35_VehicleComponentData.xlsx"

# Read the data
dataTotal <- read_excel(filename23_input, sheet = "FutuRaM-ELV")

dataComponentPetrol <- read_excel(filename35_input, sheet = "componentCarPetrol")
dataComponentDiesel <- read_excel(filename35_input, sheet = "componentCarDiesel")
dataComponentBEV <- read_excel(filename35_input, sheet = "componentCarBEV")
dataComponentHEV <- read_excel(filename35_input, sheet = "componentCarHEV")
dataComponentPHEV <- read_excel(filename35_input, sheet = "componentCarPHEV")
dataComponentOther <- read_excel(filename35_input, sheet = "componentCarOther")

```

## Start with the comparison

It is done for the year 2020. Therefore we filter the datasets first and then combine the dataset, so that we can plot them

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

dataTotal_2020 <- dataTotal %>% filter(year == 2020, productKeyLevel1 == "elvPetrol")
dataTotal_2020 <- dataTotal_2020 %>% rename(totalAl = totalAlCalculate, totalIronSteel = totalIronSteelCalculate)
dataTotal_2020 <- dataTotal_2020 %>% select(productKeyLevel2, totalAl, totalIronSteel) %>% mutate(totalMetal = totalAl + totalIronSteel, model = "total")

dataComponentPetrol_2020 <- dataComponentPetrol %>% filter(year == 2020)
dataComponentPetrol_summary <- dataComponentPetrol_2020 %>%   group_by(productKeyLevel2) %>% summarise(totalAl = sum(totalAl, na.rm = TRUE), totalIronSteel = sum(totalIronSteel)) %>%
                                  mutate(totalMetal = totalAl + totalIronSteel, model = "component")


```

## Start display different comparisions

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Combine and convert to long format
dataCheck01 <- dataTotal_2020 %>% bind_rows(dataComponentPetrol_summary) %>% pivot_longer(cols = c(totalAl, totalIronSteel, totalMetal), names_to = "metals", values_to = "values") %>%
                  mutate(error_margin = values * 0.20,  ymin = values - error_margin, ymax = values + error_margin)
dataCheck01

# Set this at the beginning of your notebook (in the setup chunk)
theme_set(
  theme_bw() +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major = element_blank(),  # Remove major grid lines
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),  # Remove minor grid lines
      text = element_text(size = 15),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 15, color = "black"),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 15, face = "bold"),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
    )
)

# First comparison for petrol cars with total Metal

dodge_width <- 0.9

p1 <- dataCheck01 %>% filter(metals == "totalMetal") %>%
      ggplot(aes(x = productKeyLevel2, y = values, fill = model)) +
      geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
      geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax), position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.25, color = "black") +
      ggtitle("Total Metal") +
      scale_y_continuous(name = "mass (kg)", limits = c(0, 2300)) +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, 
                                   vjust = 0.5,    # Vertical alignment
                                   hjust = 1),
         plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))     # Horizontal alignment

plot(p1)

ggsave("Data/Figure13A.png", plot = p1, width = 11.7, height = 8.3, units = "in", dpi = 300)

p2 <- dataCheck01 %>% filter(metals == "totalAl") %>%
        ggplot(aes(x = productKeyLevel2, y = values, fill = model)) +
          geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
          geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax), position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.25, color = "black") +
          ggtitle("Total Aluminum") +
          scale_y_continuous(name = "mass (kg)", limits = c(0, 700)) +
          theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, 
                                   vjust = 0.5,    # Vertical alignment
                                   hjust = 1),
         plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))     # Horizontal alignment

plot(p2)

ggsave("Data/Figure13B.png", plot = p2, width = 11.7, height = 8.3, units = "in", dpi = 300)

p3 <- dataCheck01 %>% filter(metals == "totalIronSteel") %>%
        ggplot(aes(x = productKeyLevel2, y = values, fill = model)) +
          geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
          geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax), position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.25, color = "black") +
          ggtitle("Total Iron and Steel") +
          scale_y_continuous(name = "mass (kg)", limits = c(0, 1700)) +
          theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, 
                                   vjust = 0.5,    # Vertical alignment
                                   hjust = 1),
         plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))     # Horizontal alignment

plot(p3)

ggsave("Data/Figure13C.png", plot = p3, width = 11.7, height = 8.3, units = "in", dpi = 300)

```
